title: Countries Where Gay Marriage Is Legal

sources.name: Same-Sex Marriage Around the World - Pew Research Center

_: Thirty-six states and the District of Columbia had legalized same-sex marriage before the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the Constitution guarantees it throughout the country.
About half of Brazil’s 27 jurisdictions had allowed same-sex marriage until a court ruling made it legal nationwide.
Same-sex marriage eventually became legal nationally after the Supreme Court declared state bans unconstitutional in 2015.
Legislation passed after then-Chancellor Angela Merkel said members of her ruling Christian Democratic Union should vote their conscience even though the party formally opposed same-sex marriage.

On March 27, 2024, the Thai parliament’s lower house passed a marriage equality bill, and on June 18, 2024, the upper house passed the bill into law. Thailand's King signed the marriage equality bill into law on September 24, 2024. The law went into effect on January 22, 2025.
Legal same-sex marriage took effect in Northern Ireland in 2020, six years after the change in England and Wales. Separate legislation was enacted in Scotland in 2014.
Then-French President François Hollande signed the law after an unsuccessful court challenge.
Only African country where same-sex marriage is legal; several countries on the continent have passed laws that ban homosexuality in recent years.
Colombia’s Constitutional Court legalized same-sex marriage by a 6-3 vote.
Became the third country globally to legalize same-sex marriage after a vote in its closely divided Parliament.
First country in Latin America to allow gay and lesbian couples to marry.
Same-sex marriage was legal in a majority of Canada’s provinces before Parliament passed national legislation.

Legal status is unclear. Although legislation officially legalizing same-sex marriage had not yet been implemented, in 2024, the federal government directed all local governments to register same-sex marriages.
Voters supported legalizing same-sex marriage by a 61.6% to 38.4% margin in a non-binding nationwide referendum.
A court ruling prompted a change in the law that made Taiwan the first jurisdiction in Asia to permit gays and lesbians to wed.
Sixth South American country to legalize same-sex marriage.
First country to legalize same-sex marriage after Parliament passed the law in December 2000.
Court ruling made Ecuador the fifth South American country to allow gays and lesbians to wed.
Second country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage, after its neighbor, the Netherlands.
Change allowing same-sex marriage was part of a broader referendum on family law that passed by a 66.9% to 33.1% vote.
Gay and lesbian couples in Sweden previously had been allowed to register for civil unions since 1995.
Measure passed by Parliament was approved by Portugal’s Constitutional Court.
In a December 2023 poll, 52% of Greek citizens supported legalization of same-sex marriages. The bill ultimately passed 175-77 on Feb.15, 2024.
A court ruling in 2017 eventually led to the change.
Nearly two-thirds of Swiss voters (64.1%) cast ballots in favor of legalizing same-sex marriage in a 2021 referendum.
Same-sex marriage became legal through a separate process in Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark, in 2016.
The law replaced a 1993 statute permitting civil unions.
The law, passed by Parliament in 2014, started out as a “citizens’ initiative” – a public petition with nearly 167,000 signatures. It came into effect in 2017.
First country to legalize same-sex marriage through a popular referendum, with more than six-in-ten Irish voters (62%) in favor.
First country in the Asia-Pacific region to allow gays and lesbians to wed.
First Central American country to legalize same-sex marriage.
Second Latin American country to legalize same-sex marriage, following Argentina.
As a US territory, Puerto Rico is bound by the laws of the U.S., where gay marriage was legalized by the U.S. Supreme Court in 2015.
First country in formerly communist Eastern Europe to legalize same-sex marriage.
Legislation legalizing marriage between same-sex couples passed 55-34 in June 2023, and the law entered into force on January 01, 2024.
The bill was championed by the country’s prime minister, Xavier Bettel, who is openly gay.
Parliament almost unanimously voted to legalize same-sex marriage.
After the law took effect, the country’s prime minister at the time, Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir, wed her longtime partner, Jónína Leósdóttir, becoming one of the first people to marry under the statute.
Parliament in this small mountain country between France and Spain voted to legalize same-sex marriage.

Same-sex marriage has been legal in Greenland since 1 April 2016. Same-sex marriage legislation passed the Inatsisartut unanimously on 26 May 2015. Approval by the Folketing followed on 19 January 2016, and the law received royal assent on 3 February
On May 16, 2024, Liechtenstein's government passed a bill in favor of marriage equality. The law went into effect January 1, 2025.
